extracted.intended_audience: aspiring fiction writers, creative-writing students, and workshop participants
extracted.subtask_description: A concise set of craft principles for writing short fiction, drawn from George Saunders's masterclass reading of seven Russian short stories; intended to guide revision, scene construction, voice, and reader experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causality is the Superpower
rubrics_metrics.description: "Causality is to the writer what melody is to the songwriter: a superpower that the audience feels as the crux of the matter."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories work when each event causes the next. Evaluate whether beats follow from prior actions/decisions rather than happening arbitrarily; prioritize causal linkage as the engine of plot and interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Escalation, Not Repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the story has moved forward through a fundamental change, that change shouldn't be enacted again. Every beat must escalate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid repeating the same change or emotional state; each scene or beat should raise the stakes, deepen complication, or alter the situation so the narrative continually moves forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Story Must "Earn Its Turn"
rubrics_metrics.description: A story has a beginning, then must turn. The turn must be set up by what came before so the reader feels its inevitability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether plot reversals, revelations, or tonal shifts are foreshadowed and grounded in prior details; an effective 'turn' feels both surprising and inevitable.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Heart-Meter Test
rubrics_metrics.description: While reading a draft, mark moments where your interest spikes (the "heart-meter"). Then ask: why did my interest spike there? Cut what flatlines. Amplify what spikes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this practical revision tool: annotate a draft with interest peaks and troughs, diagnose causes (detail, voice, causal momentum), remove dead material, and expand or replicate what generates spikes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice = Mindset
rubrics_metrics.description: "Voice is a particular style of speech, a way of putting things, a set of phrasings, tics, and cadences that suggest a particular mindset behind it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat voice as inseparable from worldview: evaluate whether phrasing, diction, and cadence consistently convey the character or narrator's mindset; use repeated phrasings/tics to sustain voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy Management
rubrics_metrics.description: You build potential energy early, convert it to kinetic energy later. Don't lose energy between beats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan where the story stores and releases narrative energy; check for lulls where energy dissipates and restructure to maintain forward thrust from setup to payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good Art = Highly Organized System
rubrics_metrics.description: "A more highly organized system is just, you know, better."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge fiction by how well its parts perform multiple functions and relate non-arbitrarily: details should simultaneously serve character, plot, theme, and texture rather than being decorative.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Reader Re-Reads Backward
rubrics_metrics.description: After finishing, the reader mentally reviews the story. A great story rewards this back-reading by revealing patterns invisible on first read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to embed patterns, echoes, and structural symmetry that enrich a second reading; ensure earlier moments gain new resonance after the story's turn or ending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honesty Over Cleverness
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshop-clever endings are usually worse than honest, slightly ungainly ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer emotionally truthful or character-driven choices over twisty cleverness; evaluate endings for honesty even if they are imperfect or awkward.

rubrics_metrics.name: The "Specificity Multiplier"
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific details perform multiple functions: they evoke sense-experience, suggest character, advance plot, build theme. Generic detail does only one thing (or none).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete, specific details that carry layered meaning; replace generic descriptors with particulars that serve sensory immediacy and deeper narrative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making the World Strange Again
rubrics_metrics.description: A great writer "estranges" the familiar so we see it new. (Shklovsky's defamiliarization.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft language, metaphors, and perspectives that render ordinary things freshly perceptible; evaluate prose for its ability to renew readers' perception of the commonplace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compassion Tax
rubrics_metrics.description: Saunders argues that the deepest story-revisions force the writer to become more compassionate toward characters they initially judged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During revision, interrogate and deepen empathy for characters: allow revisions that complicate initial judgments and create morally generative complexity rather than flattening characters into caricatures.
